conditions.displayName: storage-orphan-sweep could not sweep a tenant

documentation.content:
This alert covers the storage orphan sweep Cloud Run Job (storage-orphan-sweep-job / -dev, asia-south1).

All four conditions are threshold-on-zero: none of these counters should ever move.

## Condition 1 — aborted_total > 0

The abort counter is the one to alert on, and the reason is the opposite of the usual one. An abort means the sweep STOPPED rather than proceeded on partial knowledge, so nothing was deleted and no data is at risk. What it means is that the tool is not running, and a cleanup tool that silently stops running is exactly how orphan growth resumes unnoticed. Read the `abort_reason` label — `jsonPayload.abort_reason` on the log line the metric is extracted from:

- `reference_source_failed` — a reference source could not be enumerated, most often the Realtime Database chat walk. Check `FIREBASE_DATABASE_URL`, the service account's RTDB read permission on `tenantChat/`, and `failedSources` on `storageMaintenanceJobs/orphanSweep/tenants/{tenantId}`. This is the common one and it is a configuration or permission problem, not a data problem.
- `malformed_reference` — a stored reference value did not parse. Investigate the record before any apply run; do not raise a threshold to silence it.
- `reference_cap_exceeded` — the retain set outgrew `STORAGE_ORPHAN_SWEEP_MAX_REFERENCES`. A truncated retain set is indistinguishable from a set of orphans, so the sweep refuses to continue. Raise the ceiling deliberately, with memory in mind.
- `quarantine_cap_reached` — the per-tenant per-run move ceiling was hit. Expected on a first apply run against a backlog: the remainder is a second, deliberate run. Confirm the resume cursor is on the report document.
- `tenant_scope_violation` — non-retryable, and the serious one. A mutation point was handed a path outside the tenant's scope. Do not re-run; investigate the enumeration.

## Condition 2 — cross_tenant_references_total > 0

Expected to stay flat at zero. A cross-tenant reference is a resolved reference belonging to another tenant: it is excluded from the retain set and the run continues, so this is a data-integrity signal rather than an outage. The sweep emits one log entry per tenant run that saw at least one, with the unbounded total in `jsonPayload.value`, so as a counter metric this series counts tenant runs rather than references — both are zero together, which is all a threshold-on-zero condition needs. Read `crossTenantReferences` on the report document and find out which record points across a tenant boundary before the next apply run.

## Condition 3 — tenant_failures_total > 0

A Tenant_Sweep_Failure means this run was asked to sweep a tenant and could not: the Reference_Collector raised, or a listing page failed. Nothing was deleted for that tenant, and every OTHER tenant was still swept — the failure is confined — so this is not an outage. What it is, is the one shape in which the estate quietly stops being cleaned for a single tenant while every run looks healthy everywhere else: a tenant that is never swept is how orphan growth resumes for that tenant unnoticed. The run also exits non-zero, so the Cloud Run execution is visibly failed as well.

Read `jsonPayload.tenant_id` on the metric line, then `status`, `lastError` and `resume` on `storageMaintenanceJobs/orphanSweep/tenants/{tenantId}`. The recorded cursor and counters stand exactly as the failing attempt left them, so the next run resumes that tenant from where it stopped and skips no object — there is nothing to re-run by hand. If the same tenant fails on consecutive runs the cause is not transient: check the Realtime Database chat walk first, then the job service account’s read permissions, then that tenant’s own record shapes. Do NOT raise a ceiling or disable a reference source to clear this — a source that cannot be read is what makes a live object look orphaned.

## Condition 4 — lease_total with outcome="contended" > 0

The Run_Lease admits one execution at a time. A declined acquisition means an unexpired lease was held by another execution, so this run listed nothing, swept nothing and exited ZERO — deliberately, because another execution is doing the work and nothing was skipped. That is also exactly why it has to be alerted on rather than left to the exit code: a run that is ALWAYS declined is indistinguishable, from the report documents alone, from a run that is quietly succeeding. The reports keep updating, `aborted_total` stays flat, every execution is green — and the sweep has stopped.

One or two points here are routine: a scheduled run overlapping a manual one is the case the lease exists for. A series that never goes quiet is not. Read `storageMaintenanceJobs/orphanSweep/leases/run` — `runnerId` and `expiresAtMs` name the holder and its window, `acquiredAtIso` says when it took the lease, and `renewals` rises once per tenant, so a holder whose window keeps being extended is a run that is still working. A holder whose `expiresAtMs` is in the past is already gone and the lease self-heals: the next run acquires it, with no operator action and nothing to delete by hand. A holder whose window is live while its Cloud Run execution has finished is the case worth understanding before the next destructive run.

This condition filters on the `outcome` label, so `storage_orphan_sweep_lease_total` MUST be created with an `outcome` label extractor — the advanced `--config-from-file` form in `infra/monitoring/README.md`, not the simple counter form. Created without it the series carries no `outcome` at all and this condition can never fire, which on a threshold-on-zero condition is indistinguishable from everything being fine.

## Runbook

- Reports: Firestore `storageMaintenanceJobs/orphanSweep/tenants/{tenantId}`.
- Logs: filter on `[orphan_sweep]` and `[orphan_sweep_runner]`; counts and reasons only, no paths, filenames, emails or download tokens. The metric lines are the structured subset: `jsonPayload.metric="storage_orphan_sweep_*"`, with the delta in `jsonPayload.value`.
- In-process counters (`src/metrics.ts`, scraped over the app's `/metrics`) do NOT reach here: this is a Cloud Run job and nothing scrapes it. Every number above arrives as a log-based metric.
- Rollback: `STORAGE_ORPHAN_SWEEP_ENABLED=0`. The job becomes a no-op that does not even initialise Firebase; already-quarantined objects stay recoverable via `restoreFromQuarantine` for the retention window.
- `maxRetries: 0` on the job definition is deliberate — retrying a partially applied sweep is a human decision.

Note: like the other job policies here, these conditions read log-based metrics, so `storage_orphan_sweep_aborted_total`, `storage_orphan_sweep_cross_tenant_references_total`, `storage_orphan_sweep_tenant_failures_total` and `storage_orphan_sweep_lease_total` must exist as log-based metrics in this project before the policy can fire. Each is created over `resource.type="cloud_run_job" AND jsonPayload.metric="<name>"` — the exact commands are in `infra/monitoring/README.md`. A filter that does not match the emitted line never receives a point, which on a condition expected to hold at zero is indistinguishable from everything being fine.
